summary: Prewarm mirror commit overwrote tenant pin causing silent degraded fallback and token inflation
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary prewarm for redwood-3b-v1, the traffic-mirror commit path applied a prewarm snapshot that incorrectly wrote a namespace-level pin override. This caused ~0.3% of tenant requests from NimbusHealth to be routed to a degraded variant (rw-3b-compat-degraded) without explicit pin change in the control-plane UI. The behavior was silent; customer traffic exhibited increased token counts and slightly lower-quality outputs but no obvious 5xx.

Observed impact: Tenant experienced 22% increase in token consumption over a 40-minute window and saw a subtle regression in model outputs. Support was alerted due to spike in billing metrics and a downstream user complaint about hallucinations in summaries.
impact: Customer billing spike (approx +22% tokens during event window), small but measurable quality regression for a subset of requests, partial loss of explicit model pin semantics for tenant routing during the canary health escalation window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Schedule a canary prewarm for redwood-3b-v1 with traffic-mirror enabled and mirror_weight=0.15
2) Configure prewarm to warm both default and degraded compatibility variants
3) Trigger healthprobe escalation (induce transient latency on canary worker)
4) Observe control-plane commit logs for prewarm snapshot application and namespace-level pin writes
5) Verify tenant routing using request headers (x-tenant-id) and routed_model responses

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: prewarm mirror path incorrectly escalates a temporary probe-based health signal into a namespace pin write.
Findings:
- Prewarm commit code path (orch service) contained a branch that persisted pin metadata to etcd when mirror==true and probe_followup==true.
- The control-plane validation normally guards pins at tenant-scoped changes, but the prewarm commit uses a bypass flag for fast rollback that didn't check tenant-level manifest locks.
- Edge propagated the pin via its topology sync; no explicit UI change was visible because the pin record was written to the snapshot namespace (mirror namespace) and surfaced only in routing tables.
- Affected cohort size aligns with mirror_weight (0.12-0.18) seen in request sampling.
Open questions: Was any automated rollback triggered? (no), did quota enforcement catch the token surge? (no, because tokens were charged normally).

root_cause: Orchestrator prewarm mirror commit path bypassed tenant manifest lock and persisted a namespace-level pin when a healthprobe escalation occurred during mirror prewarm. This was caused by an optimization added in PR #1987 that didn't account for tenant-scoped pin invariants.
resolution:
Short-term workaround: Disabled traffic-mirror for scheduled prewarms for affected tenants and reverted mirror-weight on active canaries.
Permanent fix: Patch added to orchestrator to require tenant manifest lock and explicit tenant pin intent for any prewarm snapshot that writes pin metadata. Hotfix merged and scheduled for staged rollout. Billing team to review spike for potential credit.
